newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-ALBANIA PICK FOREIGN-BASED PLAYERS FOR WORLD CUP TIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALBANIA PICK FOREIGN-BASED PLAYERS FOR WORLD CUP TIES.

text.p: Albania, battered by weeks of armed anarchy, will be relying exclusively on Albanians playing for foreign clubs for their forthcoming World Cup ties against Ukraine and Germany, a senior sports official said on Monday.

Gjergj Thaka, deputy secretary-general of the Albanian Soccer Federation, said a 20-member squad was being assembled from Albanians playing abroad and he hoped it would be ready a few days before the Ukraine match on March 29.
Albania's other group nine qualifying match against Germany is due to be played on April 4.
Both fixtures are being played in Grenada, Spain, which offered itself as a neutral venue after soccer's governing body FIFA ruled out playing in Albania because of the turmoil in the country.

The trouble erupted earlier this year after rebels angry about the failure of savings schemes seized control of the south and demanded President Sali Berisha quit. The unrest spread throughout the country.
Thaka said the players would be drawn mainly from Greek and German clubs and also from Slovenia, Croatia, Romania and Malta.

For the under-21 matches against the two nations, however, all players would be drawn from teams in the Albanian soccer league, which has not played since December, including players from the south which is still in rebel hands.

Remarkably, the young players have been able to train regularly throughout the troubles, mainly in the morning, Thaka said. They are due to fly out of Albania on Tuesday, only one day after scheduled flights resumed at Tirana airport which had been closed for 11 days.
The Albanian senior team has not played since December 14, when they lost 0-2 to Ireland in Dublin. Before that they drew 1-1 with Armenia in Tirana and lost 0-3 to Portugal.

The team against Ukraine and Germany will be without one of Albania's top players, midfielder Lefter Millo who was killed earlier this month in a car accident in Greece where he played for first division Larissa.
